answer: Persistent Vertex Tagging. Each agent identity gets a graph-position fingerprint recording its interaction partners per epoch. A new identity whose fingerprint sits in a hollow region—no shared history with any prior cluster—is rate-limited and pays a per-transaction surcharge until it survives three epochs of consistent, non-random linking. Sybils must mimic real graph position across epochs, and each fake identity costs sustained fees plus coordination overhead to avoid the nebula of unflagged newcomers.
